script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'requirements-compliance',
  description: 'Check the finished application against the official wording of sections 2 to 4 of the assignment, as the company\'s evaluator would: sentence by sentence, from a clean clone',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Check', detail: 'two independent evaluators: constraints and product scope; demo data and scenarios A1-A7', model: '[REDACTED: model identifier B]' },
  ],
}

const R = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/req-check'
const REQ = R + '/requirements.txt'

const RESULT = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string', description: 'Three to six sentences: what you did and the overall verdict.' },
    requirements: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'One entry per requirement sentence (or per row/bullet) of your sections, in the order of the text.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          id: { type: 'string', description: 'e.g. "2 Backend", "3 Bulk issue (c)", "4 demo data (2)", "A6 (d)"' },
          requirement: { type: 'string', description: 'The sentence, quoted from the requirements file.' },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['met', 'partly met', 'not met', 'could not verify'] },
          evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'What you ran or looked at and what it showed: command, the relevant output, file and line, screenshot path.' },
          readme_reference: { type: 'string', description: 'Where the README documents it (section), or "not documented".' },
        },
        required: ['id', 'requirement', 'verdict', 'evidence'],
      },
    },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Every defect, gap or ambiguity you found, however small. Empty if none.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'nit'] },
          title: { type: 'string' },
          reproduction: { type: 'string', description: 'Exact steps or commands from a clean clone.' },
          expected: { type: 'string' },
          actual: { type: 'string' },
          suggestion: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['severity', 'title', 'reproduction', 'expected', 'actual'],
      },
    },
    not_checked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'requirements', 'findings', 'not_checked'],
}

const common = (name, port) => `
The candidate's submission: a clean clone at ${R}/${name}/repo (nothing installed, no database yet). Your scratch directory for scripts, downloads and screenshots: ${R}/${name}/work
The official requirements: ${REQ} (sections 2, 3 and 4 of the assignment, as the company wrote them; the layout of its tables was lost in copying, so "Area / Constraint", "Workflow / Required behavior" and "ID / Given / Expected" columns run together).
The directory ai/ and the written answers are not part of your task.

Ground rules:
- You are the company's evaluator, not the candidate's helper. Judge each sentence strictly as written. "Met" needs evidence that you produced yourself in this session; a passing test of the repository or a claim in the README is not evidence by itself.
- Work only inside your clone and your scratch directory. Do not read or change anything else on this machine: not the original repository under /home/user, nothing under /root/.claude, nothing else under the scratchpad. Do not change the candidate's code to make something pass (you may add scripts in your scratch directory).
- Network: only what "npm" needs to install the declared dependencies.
- Your port: ${port}. Another evaluator works on this machine at the same time on another port, and other jobs use the CPU: a timing can be two or three times slower than on a free machine. Before you report a timing as a failure, repeat it.
- Stop every process you start (also on failure) and check at the end that nothing of yours is still running: "pgrep -af node". This machine has no "ss" or "netstat"; a chained "sleep" in a shell command may be refused, use: python3 -c "import time; time.sleep(5)".
- A real browser is available: in a Node script, require('playwright') works from any directory and chromium.launch() needs no options. Do not install Playwright or a browser.
- Report every defect and every documentation gap, however small, with exact steps. If the wording of a requirement can be read in two ways, say which reading the submission satisfies and which not.
- Plan for about 30 minutes, then return what you have, with the rest under not_checked.`

const scope = `You evaluate a take-home submission ("Multi-Tenant Certificate Admin Console") against sections 2 and 3 of the official requirements: "Product and Technical Constraints" and "Required Product Scope".
${common('scope', '3111 (start the app with the environment variable PORT=3111, which the README documents; everything else exactly as the README says)')}

What to do:
1. Section 2, row by row.
   - Backend: language and framework (is the framework mainstream?), database (which one? is it persistent - stop the server, start it again, is the data still there? is anything of the application's state held only in memory?).
   - Frontend: Vue 3 or React.
   - Startup: "One documented command must install or use declared dependencies, initialize demo data, and start the complete app." Run exactly the documented command in the clean clone and time it; confirm that after it the complete app (UI and API) answers and the demo data is there. Is it one command? "A second command may run verification": run it once near the end and report the result (it takes one to three minutes on this machine).
   - Actor context: no login UI; one admin seeded per tenant; how is the actor identified (header or token)? What happens without it, and with an unknown actor?
   - Scope control: look through the code and the UI for production authentication, cloud deployment, notifications or unrelated features. "Correct core behavior comes before visual polish": say if you see polish that displaced correctness.
2. Section 3, workflow by workflow, in a real browser against the running app, as a user:
   - Certificate list: select an actor; search by learner name; search by serial number; paginate; sort (each sortable column, both directions). Provoke and observe the loading state, the empty state and the error state (for example: a search with no result; intercept or delay the list request in the browser; stop the server and act in the UI).
   - Bulk issue: choose a course and issue to all eligible learners. Is a duplicate submission disabled in the UI (double click, Enter held down, clicking again while the first request is delayed)? Is the operation status shown? Are per-learner outcomes returned and shown: issued, skipped, failed - and for skipped and failed, the reason?
   - Certificate detail: serial number, course, learner, tenant-local issue date, status. Revocation with confirmation (can it be revoked without confirming? what does cancel do?). "Audit both issuance and revocation": where can an evaluator see the audit events, and is there exactly one per issuance and per revocation?
   - CSV export: columns learner name, course title, serial number, tenant-local issue date. "Preserve current search and sort": set a search and a sort in the UI, export from the UI, and compare the file with what the list shows (same rows, same order). "Handle 100,000-row exports as specified in A6" is checked by the other evaluator; you only confirm that the UI's export works on the demo data.
3. Take a screenshot of each state you report on (file names in your scratch directory).

Return one entry per requirement sentence of sections 2 and 3, and every finding.`

const scenarios = `You evaluate a take-home submission ("Multi-Tenant Certificate Admin Console") against section 4 of the official requirements: "Acceptance Scenarios" - the required demo data and the scenarios A1 to A7.
${common('scenarios', '3000 (the default; start the app exactly as the README says, and copy the README\'s commands verbatim)')}

The company writes: "Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario" and "We will run our own checks against your API and UI." Do both, in this order:

Part 1 - the README's own reproduction steps. Start from the clean clone with the one documented command. For each scenario A1 to A7, follow the README's steps exactly as written (copy and paste the commands). Report every step that fails, prints something else than the README says, is ambiguous, needs knowledge the README does not give, or does not actually demonstrate what the "Expected" column of the scenario says.

Part 2 - your own checks, as the company would run them. Do not reuse the repository's tests. Design an independent check of each scenario's "Given" and "Expected" against the API (curl, or Node scripts in your scratch directory) and, where a scenario speaks of what is displayed, against the UI in a real browser. Treat the wording of "Expected" as the contract:
- Required demo data: the two tenants and their time zones; the two admins, each bound only to their own tenant; in both tenants a course titled "Safety 101" and a learner named "Alex Lee"; completed, incomplete and already certified enrollments; a command or script that generates 100,000 certificate rows for one tenant "without changing the default quick-start dataset" - establish what that means here and whether it holds (what does a fresh clone, or a reset, show before and after?).
- A1: Bob against East data through the list, detail, bulk issue and export endpoints: only West data is accessible; a cross-tenant detail request returns 404 or an equivalent non-revealing response (compare it with the response for an id that does not exist at all - can Bob tell the difference?); a cross-tenant bulk issue is rejected and creates no certificates and no audit events (count both before and after).
- A2: the same bulk request with the same idempotency key, sequentially and concurrently (for example twenty at once, more than once): one logical operation; each eligible learner receives at most one certificate; each actual issuance has exactly one audit event; all callers receive the outcome of the same logical operation; no additional certificates or audit events.
- A3: the same key with a different course, and with a different payload: 409; no second operation; the first result is not overwritten (replay the original request afterwards).
- A4: a course with completed, incomplete and already certified learners: issued only to eligible learners; incomplete and duplicate cases skipped with reasons.
- A5: an East certificate and a West certificate with the UTC timestamp 2026-01-10T13:30:00Z: East displays 2026-01-11 00:30, West displays 2026-01-10 21:30 (in the API and in the UI); list sorting and CSV use the tenant-local calendar date (find or create certificates around a local midnight and check the order and the CSV dates). How does an evaluator get certificates with exactly this timestamp - is that documented?
- A6: generate 100,000 East certificates with the documented command, including rows with equal values for the requested sort field; apply a search and a sort; run the export twice; during the first export request the certificate list. Each export completes within 60 seconds; the CSV contains exactly the matching East rows in the requested order (verify the set and the order independently, for example with your own query on the SQLite file or by paging through the list API); rows with equal sort keys appear in the same relative order in both exports (compare the two files byte for byte, and look at a stretch of equal keys); the list request succeeds while the export is running (measure when it was sent and answered relative to the export). Try more than one combination of search and sort, including a sort by the local issue date and one with many equal keys.
- A7: Alice revokes a valid certificate, then repeats the request: the first request changes the status and writes one revocation audit event; the repeat creates no duplicate audit event (also when the two requests are sent at the same moment).

Return one entry per demo-data bullet and per sentence of each scenario's "Expected" column, plus one entry per scenario for "the README explains how to reproduce it", and every finding.`

phase('Check')
const names = ['scope', 'scenarios']
const results = await parallel([scope, scenarios].map((prompt, i) => () =>
  agent(prompt, { label: `evaluate:${names[i]}`, phase: 'Check', schema: RESULT, model: '[REDACTED: model identifier B]' })))
const out = {}
results.forEach((r, i) => { out[names[i]] = r })
const verdicts = results.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => (r.requirements || []).map(x => x.verdict))
const count = v => verdicts.filter(x => x === v).length
log(`requirements: ${verdicts.length} checked - met ${count('met')}, partly met ${count('partly met')}, not met ${count('not met')}, could not verify ${count('could not verify')}; findings: ${results.filter(Boolean).reduce((n, r) => n + (r.findings || []).length, 0)}`)
return out

scope.summary: I ran exactly `PORT=3111 npm start` in the clean clone. It installed the dependencies, built the React UI, created the SQLite demo database and served both UI and API in about 5 s (with a warm npm cache). I then tested every workflow of section 3 in real Chromium with Playwright: actor switching, search by name and serial, paging, sorting every column both ways, and loading, empty and error states (delayed or failed requests, stopped server). I also tested bulk issue: double-click, repeated Enter, forced re-click, a lost answer followed by a safe retry, and a failed outcome caused by a fault I injected into the database. On the detail drawer I checked the fields, cancel, Escape and confirmed revocation, and the audit events in the drawer, the API and the database. For CSV export I exported three search and sort combinations from the UI and compared each file with the list on screen. A stop and restart showed the data persists. `npm test` passed once (193 API and 257 UI tests, exit 0, 79 s). Every requirement sentence of sections 2 and 3 that was in my scope is met. The 100,000-row part of the export row is left to the other evaluator. I found only nits: the Loading badge covers the Status column header, failed outcomes give a generic reason, the CSV date includes a time, and two rows show the same local time at the DST change with nothing to tell them apart.

requirements.requirement: Go, Python, or Node with a mainstream framework.
requirements.evidence: backend/package.json: express ^5.1.0; backend/src/app.js is an Express app run by node backend/src/server.js (Node v22.23.5). Express is mainstream.

requirements.requirement: Use SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL.
requirements.evidence: /api/health answered {"status":"ok","database":"better-sqlite3"}. File repo/data/cert-admin.sqlite created; schema in backend/src/db/schema.js (tenants, admins, courses, learners, enrollments, bulk_issue_operations, certificates, audit_events).

requirements.requirement: An in-memory store is not sufficient.
requirements.evidence: I revoked certificate 5 and ran bulk operations 1 to 3, then stopped the server (SIGTERM to its node process) and started it again with PORT=3111 npm start. The certificate was still revoked with reason 'evaluator test', and GET /api/bulk-issues still listed the operations with their idempotency keys. sqlite.js refuses ':memory:'. grep found in-memory Maps only for a socket-watcher set, prepared statements and a date-format cache. No application state is kept only in memory, except the browser's sessionStorage for unresolved bulk attempts, which is a client-side convenience.
requirements.readme_reference: Section 1: 'Data lives in data/cert-admin.sqlite and survives restarts'

requirements.requirement: Vue 3 or React. Vite is optional.
requirements.evidence: frontend/package.json has react ^19.2.0 and vite ^8; the build output during npm start was 'vite v8.3.8 building client environment'.

requirements.requirement: One documented command must install or use declared dependencies, initialize demo data, and start the complete app.
requirements.evidence: I ran `PORT=3111 npm start` in the clean clone (no node_modules, no DB). Log: 'added 176 packages in 3s', vite build, 'Created demo data in .../data/cert-admin.sqlite', 'listening on http://localhost:3111'. /api/health answered after 5.0 s (npm cache warm). GET / returned 200 text/html, and the UI showed 7 East certificates. GET /api/actors listed alice@east.test (East, Australia/Sydney) and bob@west.test (West, Australia/Perth). Later restarts were up in 1.5 s and kept the data. It is a single command (log in work/start.log).

requirements.requirement: A second command may run verification.
requirements.evidence: I ran `npm test` once with the server stopped: exit 0 after 79 s. API: tests 193, pass 193, fail 0, skipped 0. UI: Test Files 9 passed, Tests 257 passed. The app database was unchanged afterwards: cert 5 still revoked, 16 certificates (log in work/test.log).

requirements.requirement: No login UI is needed.
requirements.evidence: The UI opens straight on the certificate list with an 'Acting as' select (screenshot work/01-initial.png). There is no login form. grep for login/password/jwt/oauth in backend/src and frontend/src found nothing.

requirements.requirement: Seed one admin per tenant
requirements.evidence: GET /api/actors returns exactly alice@east.test (East) and bob@west.test (West). As Bob, opening #/certificates/1 (East) in the UI shows 'Certificate not found ... It may belong to another tenant' (work/27-bob-east-detail.png).

requirements.requirement: identify the actor with a header or token.
requirements.evidence: Header X-Actor-Email. In the browser, every /api request carried x-actor-email of the selected actor. Without the header: 401 {code: actor_required}. With 'eve@x.test': 401 {code: unknown_actor}. 'ALICE@east.test' is accepted case-insensitively. An unknown actor stored in localStorage ('cert-admin.actor' = eve@nowhere.test) falls back to alice on reload (work/28-unknown-stored-actor.png).

requirements.requirement: Do not add production authentication, cloud deployment, notifications, or unrelated features.
requirements.evidence: grep for auth, notification, smtp, docker, aws, vercel and heroku in backend/src and frontend/src found nothing. The repo has no Dockerfile, CI config or deploy files. The only extras are a status filter, a Recent operations table, a roster preview and an audit-events endpoint, all directly tied to the required workflows.

requirements.requirement: Correct core behavior comes before visual polish.
requirements.evidence: Every core behaviour I tested in the browser worked (see section 3 entries). The styling is plain and functional. I saw no polish that displaced correctness; the only visual flaw is the Loading badge covering a header (nit finding).

requirements.requirement: Select an actor
requirements.evidence: Choosing bob@west.test in 'Acting as' reloaded the list with WEST-0000001..4, and the header changed to 'West / Australia/Perth'. Switching back showed East. Requests carried the new header (work/02-west-actor.png).

requirements.requirement: search by learner name or serial number
requirements.evidence: 'alex' and 'LEE' both return only EAST-0000001 Alex Lee (work/03-search-name.png). 'EAST-0000004' returns only that row (work/04-search-serial.png), and the partial '0000005' returns EAST-0000005. Typing is debounced into a single request, e.g. q=alex.

requirements.requirement: paginate
requirements.evidence: With rows per page 5: page 1 shows 7..3 and '1–5 of 7'. Next goes to page 2 (rows 2, 1, '6–7 of 7') and Next is then disabled. Previous returns to page 1. Requests used page=2&pageSize=5 (work/06-page2.png).

requirements.requirement: and sort.
requirements.evidence: I clicked each header twice: serial asc/desc, learner asc/desc, course asc/desc, issued desc/asc, status asc/desc. Each click sent sort=<col>&order=<dir>, aria-sort matched, and the row order was correct (screenshots work/07-sort-*.png).

requirements.requirement: Show loading, empty, and error states.
requirements.evidence: Loading: with the list request delayed 3 s, the first load shows 'Loading certificates…' (work/08b-initial-loading.png). On later loads the old rows stay with a 'Loading…' badge and aria-busy=true (work/08-loading.png). Empty: q=zzzz-nomatch shows 'No certificates match your search' with a 'Clear search and filters' button (work/05-empty.png). Error: an intercepted 500 shows 'Certificates could not be loaded / boom / HTTP 500 · internal_error / Try again' (work/09-error-500.png). An aborted request shows 'The server could not be reached' (work/10-error-network.png), and Try again recovers. A real server stop gives the same message in the list (work/22-server-down-list.png), the export (work/23) and the bulk page (work/24).

requirements.requirement: Choose a course and issue to all eligible learners.
requirements.evidence: East Safety 101 roster: 2 eligible. 'Issue 2 certificates' issued EAST-0000008 (Marcus O'Connor) and EAST-0000009 (Priya Sharma) and skipped Alex Lee (already_certified), Mei Chen and Tom Walker (not_completed) (work/12-bulk-roster.png, work/14-bulk-result.png). First Aid Refresher issued 1 (Alex Lee) and skipped 4, including the revoked case.

requirements.requirement: Disable duplicate UI submission
requirements.evidence: With the POST delayed 4 s, I double-clicked the button, clicked it again, pressed Enter 10 times plus a held Enter, and forced a click through JS after setting disabled=false. Exactly 1 POST was sent (one idempotency key). Button and course select were disabled while in flight. When the answer was lost (connection reset after the server processed it), the UI showed 'may or may not have gone through', locked the course, and 'Retry safely' resent the same key. The server replayed operation #4 and nothing was issued twice (work/25-bulk-lost-answer.png, work/26-bulk-retried.png).

requirements.requirement: and show operation status.
requirements.evidence: In flight: button 'Issuing…' plus a live region 'Issuing certificates for First Aid Refresher… Please wait; the button is locked until the server has answered.' (work/13-bulk-inflight.png). Done: 'Operation #2 for First Aid Refresher completed: 1 issued, 4 skipped, 0 failed', a status card and a Recent operations table.

requirements.requirement: Return per-learner outcomes: issued, skipped, or failed.
requirements.evidence: The response and the UI table list each learner. Issued rows give the certificate serial and local time. Skipped rows give a reason: 'Already certified (certificate EAST-0000001)', 'Course not completed (enrollment is in progress)', or 'Certificate EAST-0000002 was revoked...'. Failed: I injected a SQLite trigger that aborts the certificate insert for West learner Emily Davis (removed afterwards). Op #3 showed '1 issued, 3 skipped, 1 failed', and Emily Davis was 'Failed: The certificate could not be issued because of an unexpected error ... the server log has the details', with reason code issue_failed. The server log had the real cause (work/15-bulk-failed-outcome.png).

requirements.requirement: Show serial number, course, learner, tenant-local issue date, and status.
requirements.evidence: The drawer for EAST-0000005 shows serial, 'Active' badge, learner Priya Sharma, course Forklift Operations, 'ISSUE DATE (AUSTRALIA/SYDNEY) 2026-06-15 12:00 UTC+10:00' plus the UTC instant, and the issuer (work/16-detail.png). A bulk-issued certificate also shows 'bulk operation #1' (work/20-detail-bulk-issued.png).

requirements.requirement: Support revocation with confirmation.
requirements.evidence: 'Revoke certificate…' opens a modal 'Revoke this certificate?' with an optional reason; opening it sends 0 POSTs (work/17-revoke-confirm.png). Cancel and Escape both close it with 0 POSTs, and the certificate stays Active (work/18-after-cancel.png). Double-clicking the confirm button sent exactly 1 POST. Afterwards the drawer shows 'The certificate has been revoked', Revoked, the revoked time, who revoked it and the reason (work/19-revoked-detail.png). A repeated API revoke returns alreadyRevoked:true.

requirements.requirement: Audit both issuance and revocation.
requirements.evidence: The detail drawer shows the audit trail with 'Certificate issued by…' and 'Certificate revoked by… reason: evaluator test'. GET /api/audit-events?certificateId=5 gives exactly 1 issued and 1 revoked event, and after a repeat revoke the revoked count is still 1. Database: 15 certificates had exactly 15 certificate.issued events, no certificate lacked one, no (certificate, action) pair was duplicated, and the failed learner got no event.

requirements.requirement: Export learner name, course title, serial number, and tenant-local issue date.
requirements.evidence: UI download certificates-east-20261124-2206.csv has the header 'Learner Name,Course Title,Serial Number,Issue Date (Australia/Sydney)' and rows such as 'Alex Lee,Safety 101,EAST-0000001,2026-01-11 00:30'. The date is tenant-local and includes HH:mm (see the nit finding).

requirements.requirement: Preserve current search and sort.
requirements.evidence: Three UI exports: q='a' with Learner Z to A (10 rows); q='EAST-00000' with Course A to Z (10 rows); no search with Issue date oldest first (10 rows). For each, the CSV rows were identical in content and order to the list on screen (100 rows per page) (work/csv1.csv, csv2.csv, csv3.csv, work/21-export-*.png). Request: export.csv?q=a&status=all&sort=learner&order=desc.

requirements.requirement: Handle 100,000-row exports as specified in A6.
requirements.evidence: Assigned to the other evaluator. I only confirmed that the UI export works on the demo data (above).

findings.title: List 'Loading…' badge covers the STATUS column header
findings.reproduction: PORT=3111 npm start; in Chromium, delay GET /api/certificates?* by 3 s (route interception), then type 'a' in Search on the Certificates page.
findings.expected: The loading indicator does not hide table content.
findings.actual: The 'Loading…' pill sits over the STATUS header, which reads 'ST'. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/req-check/scope/work/08-loading.png
findings.suggestion: Place the indicator outside the header row, or reserve space for it.

findings.title: Failed per-learner outcome gives only a generic reason
findings.reproduction: While the server runs, add a SQLite trigger on data/cert-admin.sqlite: CREATE TRIGGER eval_fail BEFORE INSERT ON certificates WHEN NEW.learner_id=10 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'x'); END; then, as bob, bulk issue West Safety 101 in the UI.
findings.expected: Reading 1: 'failed' needs a reason, like 'skipped'. Reading 2: the requirement only names the outcomes issued, skipped and failed.
findings.actual: Emily Davis shows outcome Failed, reason code issue_failed, and a generic message ('unexpected error ... the server log has the details'). The actual cause is only in the server log. This satisfies reading 2, and reading 1 only with a generic reason. Screenshot work/15-bulk-failed-outcome.png
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as is; could expose a safe classification of the cause.

findings.title: CSV 'tenant-local issue date' column contains date and time
findings.reproduction: In the UI, click Export CSV and open the file.
findings.expected: 'Tenant-local issue date' (and A5's 'CSV use the tenant-local calendar date') can be read as date only (YYYY-MM-DD) or as a local date-time.
findings.actual: The column is 'Issue Date (Australia/Sydney)' with values like '2026-01-11 00:30'. The tenant-local calendar date is correct, but the time is included. This satisfies the date-time reading, not a strict date-only reading.
findings.suggestion: Document the choice, or add a separate date-only column.

findings.title: Two different instants show the same local time in the list at the DST end, with no way to tell them apart
findings.reproduction: As alice, view the Certificates list sorted by Issue date.
findings.expected: Rows with distinct instants are distinguishable in the list (for example by offset), or are knowingly shown as equal.
findings.actual: EAST-0000003 (2026-04-04T15:30Z) and EAST-0000004 (16:30Z) both show '2026-04-05 02:30'. Only the detail drawer shows UTC+11:00 versus UTC+10:00. The sort order is correct (by instant).
findings.suggestion: Show the offset in the list for ambiguous local times.

not_checked: The 100,000-row export (A6), which is assigned to the other evaluator
Startup time with a cold npm cache: the 5 s I measured used a warm cache on this machine
A true OS-level held Enter key with auto-repeat (I simulated 10 Enter presses plus a keydown/keyup)
Browsers other than Chromium, and screen readers
npm run dev, npm run db:reset and generate:east

scenarios.summary: I started the clean clone with `npm start` (port 3000) and followed every step of the README section "Reproducing A1–A7 by hand". I ran the commands verbatim, with one change: I wrote the /tmp output files to my scratch directory instead. Every output matched what the README says. I then ran my own checks: Node and curl scripts, my own read-only SQLite queries, and Playwright in Chromium for the UI. The demo data and A1, A2, A3, A4, A6 and A7 met the Expected column, including concurrent bursts and a byte-for-byte comparison of the exports against an independent query. A5 passed: the API, UI and CSV show 2026-01-11 00:30 (East) and 2026-01-10 21:30 (West). Local-date ordering is correct on certificates I inserted around midnight myself, but an evaluator cannot reproduce that ordering on the running app; the README sends them to the candidate's own test instead. All defects I found are documentation gaps or nits, and none breaks a requirement. The one point that depends on interpretation is "without changing the default quick-start dataset": the seeded rows stay unchanged row for row, but the default command writes into the quick-start database, so the console then shows 100,007 East certificates and 10 extra courses until `--clear` or `db:reset` is run.

requirements.requirement: Tenant East using Australia/Sydney and West using Australia/Perth.
requirements.evidence: Fresh DB after `npm start`: tenants table rows (1,'East','EAST','Australia/Sydney') and (2,'West','WEST','Australia/Perth'); GET /api/me as alice returns tenant East/Australia/Sydney, as bob returns West/Australia/Perth; UI header shows 'East Australia/Sydney'.

requirements.requirement: Admins alice@east.test and bob@west.test, each bound only to their own tenant.
requirements.evidence: admins table: alice tenant_id 1, bob tenant_id 2 (one tenant column, email unique). The tenant cannot be overridden: Bob's list with ?tenant=East, ?tenantId=1 and headers X-Tenant: East / X-Tenant-Id: 1 still returned only the 4 WEST certificates; body fields tenant/tenantId on bulk issue were ignored (404 for East course).

requirements.requirement: Both tenants contain a course titled Safety 101 and a learner named Alex Lee.
requirements.evidence: GET /api/courses/1/enrollments (alice) and /api/courses/4/enrollments (bob) both have course title 'Safety 101' and a learner 'Alex Lee' (learner ids 1 and 8).

requirements.requirement: Include completed, incomplete, and already certified enrollments.
requirements.evidence: Safety 101 rosters (my own SQL join of enrollments/learners/certificates): East Alex Lee completed+cert 1, Priya/Marcus completed no cert, Mei in_progress, Tom not_started; West Alex Lee completed+cert 8, Jordan/Emily completed, Noah in_progress, Grace not_started. The roster API reports 'already_certified' and 'not_completed' the same way. West also has a revoked certificate (Grace Kim, Working at Heights).

requirements.requirement: A command or script that can generate 100,000 certificate rows for one tenant without changing the default quick-start dataset.
requirements.evidence: `npm run generate:east` took 3.3-3.8 s and added exactly 100,000 East certificates. My dump script (work/dump.py) hashed every non-generated row of tenants, admins, courses, learners, enrollments, certificates, audit_events and bulk_issue_operations before generating, after generating and after `--clear`: all hashes were identical, including tenants.last_serial. `--clear` brings the counts back to 11 certificates and 13 audit events. `--db <file>` generates into a separate file (it created a seeded copy plus the 100k rows in work/load.sqlite). Reading 1 (the seeded rows are not modified): met. Reading 2 (the quick-start app is unchanged): not met by the default command. It writes into data/cert-admin.sqlite, so GET /api/certificates for Alice then reports total 100,007 instead of 7. The course picker and /api/courses gain 10 '(load test)' courses. The default list (issued desc) puts generated rows first. This lasts until `--clear` or `npm run db:reset`.

requirements.requirement: Only West data is accessible.
requirements.evidence: work/a1.mjs as Bob: list (no params, ?tenant=East, ?tenantId=1, ?q=EAST, ?q=Priya, status=all) only ever showed WEST-0000001..4 or 0 rows. Export (no params, ?q=EAST, ?tenant=East, ?q=Priya) contained no EAST serial and no East learner. Bob also got 404 for: revoke of East cert 3, GET /api/bulk-issues/<East op id>, GET /api/courses/1/enrollments. GET /api/audit-events?certificateId=1 returned an empty list. UI as Bob: list shows only the 4 WEST rows and the body text has no 'EAST-'.

requirements.requirement: A cross-tenant detail request returns 404 or an equivalent non-revealing response.
requirements.evidence: Bob GET /api/certificates/1, 2, 3, 7 -> 404 {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"Certificate not found"}}. I compared status, body and all headers except Date with GET /api/certificates/999999: identical. Median latency over 30 requests: 1.20 ms (cross-tenant) vs 1.31 ms (missing), so Bob cannot tell the two apart. UI: Bob opening #/certificates/1 and #/certificates/999999 both show 'Certificate not found' (screenshot work/ui-a1-bob-east-cert.png).

requirements.requirement: Cross-tenant bulk issue is rejected and creates no certificates or audit events.
requirements.evidence: Bob POST /api/bulk-issues returned 404 'Course not found' for each of: {courseId:1}, {courseId:2}, {course_id:1}, {courseId:1,tenant:'East'}, {courseId:1,tenantId:1}, a nonexistent course, and Alice's own key with her East course. My SQL counts per tenant were identical before and after: certificates [[1,7],[2,4]], audit_events [[1,8],[2,5]], bulk_issue_operations [[1,1]]. East certificate statuses were unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A1).
requirements.evidence: Ran all 12 README A1 commands after `npm run db:reset`. Outputs matched every comment: 7 EAST, 4 WEST, export 4 WEST, two identical 404 bodies, 404 Course not found, totals 7/8/{"items":[]} and 4/5/{"items":[]}. The UI step (#/certificates/1 as Bob) showed 'Certificate not found'.

requirements.requirement: One logical operation.
requirements.evidence: work/a2.mjs, 3 rounds, each on a freshly reset DB. Each round: 3 sequential requests with one key, then two bursts of 20 concurrent requests with another key. After each round there are exactly 2 bulk_issue_operations rows (one per key), and every response body carries the same operation id. README steps gave the same result: '2 operations'.

requirements.requirement: Each eligible learner receives at most one certificate.
requirements.evidence: In all rounds, SQL `select course_id,learner_id,count(*) ... having n>1` returned 0 rows. Certificates went 7 -> 8 -> 10 -> 10 (no change after the second burst). An extra test sent 20 concurrent requests with 20 different keys on Safety 101: 2 certificates issued in total, no duplicates.

requirements.requirement: Each actual issuance has exactly one audit event.
requirements.evidence: In every round, SQL counting certificates without exactly one 'certificate.issued' event returned 0. The issued certificate ids [13,14] had event counts [[13,1],[14,1]], and the issued-event total equals the certificate count (10).

requirements.requirement: All callers receive the outcome of the same logical operation, without additional certificates or audit events.
requirements.evidence: All 40 concurrent responses per round: status 201 and one distinct body (byte-identical), with exactly one response 'Idempotent-Replayed: false' and the rest true. The 3 sequential responses were byte-identical (201 false, then 201 true twice). Counts did not change after the replay bursts.

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A2).
requirements.evidence: README outputs reproduced exactly: 201 false, then 201 true twice; then 20 / 1 / 2 / total 10 / total 10. One caveat: the steps write to and delete /tmp/a2-*.json (see finding); I ran them with a scratch path instead.

requirements.requirement: Return 409.
requirements.evidence: After key k3 had been used for {courseId:1}, the same key returned 409 idempotency_key_reused for each of: {courseId:2}, {courseId:3}, {courseId:1,note:'x'}, {courseId:'1'}, {courseId:1,learnerIds:[2]}, {}, 'notjson', {courseId:4} (West course), {courseId:999}. 10 concurrent misuse requests all returned 409. {courseId:1.0} and '{ "courseId" : 1 }' were treated as the same request and replayed. That is a defensible reading, since the JSON values are equal.

requirements.requirement: Do not execute a second operation or overwrite the first result.
requirements.evidence: After all the misuse requests the DB still had certificates 13, audit 15 and ops 1. The stored request_hash and response_body were unchanged. Replaying the original {courseId:1} with key k3 gave a body byte-identical to the first response (cmp), with Idempotent-Replayed: true.

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A3).
requirements.evidence: README steps gave '409 idempotency_key_reused', 'first result intact' and 'still 2 operations', as documented. They only show the 'different course' case, not a different payload for the same course (the scenario says 'different course or request payload'); I verified that case myself.

requirements.requirement: Certificates are issued only to eligible learners.
requirements.evidence: East Safety 101: only Marcus O'Connor and Priya Sharma were issued (README run and UI). West Safety 101 (Bob, my own run): only Emily Davis and Jordan Smith were issued. A second run with a new key issued 0 (5 skipped). On West Working at Heights only Alex Lee (completed, uncertified) was issued. UI: the roster preview says 'Will be issued' for exactly those 2, and a triple-click on Issue sent a single POST.

requirements.requirement: Incomplete and duplicate cases are skipped with reasons.
requirements.evidence: Results carry outcome 'skipped' with reason and message. not_completed: 'Course not completed (enrollment is in progress/not started)'. already_certified: 'Already certified (certificate WEST-0000001)'. certificate_revoked: 'Certificate WEST-0000003 was revoked; ...'. The UI result table shows the same text (screenshot work/ui-a4-bulk.png).

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A4).
requirements.evidence: The node one-liner printed exactly the documented summary and 5 lines (serials EAST-0000009/10 as documented).

requirements.requirement: East displays 2026-01-11 00:30.
requirements.evidence: API detail of cert 1: issuedAt 2026-01-10T13:30:00.000Z, issuedLocal '2026-01-11 00:30'. The CSV row prints 2026-01-11 00:30. UI list row and detail drawer show '2026-01-11 00:30 UTC+11:00' (screenshot work/ui-a5-east-detail.png).

requirements.requirement: West displays 2026-01-10 21:30.
requirements.evidence: API detail of cert 8: issuedLocal '2026-01-10 21:30'. The CSV prints 2026-01-10 21:30. UI list and drawer show '2026-01-10 21:30 UTC+08:00' (work/ui-a5-west-detail.png).

requirements.requirement: List sorting and CSV use the tenant-local calendar date.
requirements.evidence: I inserted directly into the DB (bypassing the app) two East certs on the same UTC day: P (lower id) at 2026-03-01T14:00Z, which is Sydney 03-02, and Q (higher id) at 2026-03-01T12:00Z, which is Sydney 03-01. I did the same for West around Perth midnight. The list (sort=issued asc/desc) and the CSV both order Q before P (asc) and print 2026-03-01 23:00 / 2026-03-02 01:00. A UTC-date-then-id order would give P first. Independently, issued_local_date of all 100,009 East certificates (seeded plus generated, spanning both DSTs) equals my own Intl Sydney date: 0 mismatches. CSV dates of every exported row equal my own Intl computation: 0 mismatches in the a6.mjs runs.

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A5).
requirements.evidence: The README conversion steps work: the seeded certs 1 and 8 have exactly 2026-01-10T13:30Z, as documented in section 2. The README itself says these lines do not show the ordering rule, and sends the evaluator to the candidate's own test (`node --test ... 'tenant-local calendar date'`, which passed in 0.5 s). There is no documented way to create certificates at chosen instants on the running app, so the ordering part cannot be reproduced through the API or UI.

requirements.requirement: Each export completes within 60 seconds.
requirements.evidence: work/a6.mjs, 7 search/sort combinations run twice each (14 exports), plus README runs and a UI export. Slowest: 435 ms (25,480 rows). Full 100,010-row course sort: 422 ms and 318 ms. UI export: 507 ms.

requirements.requirement: The CSV contains exactly the matching East rows in the requested order.
requirements.evidence: For q=an/learner desc, q=lee/issued asc, no q/course asc, q=ma/status desc, q=EAST-LT-00/issued desc, status=revoked/issued asc and q=zz-nothing/serial asc: the serial set equalled my own query on the SQLite file (substring of the folded name or the serial), with 0 missing, 0 extra and no duplicates. Sort keys were monotone in the requested direction (0 violations), and names and dates matched the DB. Paging through the list API (pageSize 100) gave exactly the CSV serial order for 3 more combinations. The UI export (search 'an', Learner Z to A) is byte-identical to the API export.

requirements.requirement: Rows with equal sort keys appear in the same relative order on repeated exports.
requirements.evidence: Both exports were byte-identical (Buffer.equals) for all 7 combinations. The longest runs of equal keys covered: 10,000 rows (course), 9,480 (status), 400 (issued local date), 110 (learner name). The README and UI exports also matched an earlier export of the same query byte for byte.

requirements.requirement: The certificate list request succeeds while the export is running.
requirements.evidence: For each combination a list request was sent once the first export chunk had arrived. Example: export sent at 0 ms, list sent at 50 ms, answered 200 with 50 items at 78 ms, export finished at 435 ms. Every combination shows sent < answered < export end. In the browser: the list request was sent at 1909 ms and done at 1931 ms, while the export ran from 1888 ms to 2395 ms.

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A6).
requirements.evidence: The README steps worked (generate 3.8 s; exports 0.51 s and 0.37 s; cmp identical; 25,481 lines; 'ties in ascending id order'; six list timings of 5-8 ms). However, the list-during-export step prints no export start/end times, so it does not show that the list requests overlapped the exports. Nothing checks the CSV row set against the data.

requirements.requirement: The first request changes status and writes one revocation audit event.
requirements.evidence: Cert 4: before ('active', no revoke events). The first POST /revoke {reason:'first'} returned 200 with status revoked and alreadyRevoked false; the DB showed revoked, revoked_at set, reason 'first', 1 revoke event, all events 13 -> 14. UI: revoking EAST-0000005 through the confirmation dialog shows 'The certificate has been revoked.' and a 'Certificate revoked by alice@east.test' audit entry (work/ui-a7-revoked.png).

requirements.requirement: The repeat does not create duplicate audit events.
requirements.evidence: Repeat with reason 'second': 200, alreadyRevoked true, reason stays 'first', revoke events still 1, total events still 14. Concurrency: 20 simultaneous revokes on each of certs 5, 6 and 7 -> 60 x 200, exactly 1 revoke event per certificate, total events +1 per certificate.

requirements.requirement: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A7).
requirements.evidence: Outputs matched every comment: active / false / revoked / true / 1 issued + 1 revoked event. The UI instruction works as described.

findings.title: Default generator command changes what the quick-start console shows
findings.reproduction: Fresh clone: `npm start`; in a second terminal `npm run generate:east`; `curl -s -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' 'http://localhost:3000/api/certificates?pageSize=1'` and `curl -s -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' http://localhost:3000/api/courses`
findings.expected: Under the stricter reading of 'without changing the default quick-start dataset', the quick-start app still shows its 7 East certificates and 3 courses.
findings.actual: total 100007. /api/courses lists 10 extra '(load test)' courses, and the default list (newest first) shows generated rows ahead of the demo rows. The seeded rows themselves are byte-identical (verified by hashing), and `--clear`, `db:reset` or `--db <other file>` restore the original view.
findings.suggestion: Make generating into a separate file the default (or the documented primary path), or state explicitly that 'quick-start dataset' means the seeded rows, not what the running console shows.

findings.title: A5 ordering rule cannot be reproduced on the running app
findings.reproduction: README › Reproducing A5: the curl lines only show the conversion; the README says the ordering case is 'built and checked ... by one test of the suite' and gives `(cd backend && node --test ... --test-name-pattern='tenant-local calendar date' test/acceptance.test.js)`
findings.expected: An evaluator can see, through the API and UI, that list sorting and CSV use the tenant-local date (e.g. seeded certificates on the same UTC day but different local days, or a documented way to create them).
findings.actual: No seeded pair shows the difference, and there is no documented way to create certificates at a chosen instant. Reproducing it means trusting the candidate's own test. I had to insert rows directly into SQLite to check it (it does sort correctly).
findings.suggestion: Seed one pair per tenant around local midnight (lower id issued later in UTC), or document a script that inserts them.

findings.title: README reproduction steps write to and delete shared /tmp paths
findings.reproduction: README › Reproducing A2/A3/A6: `rm -f /tmp/a2-*.json`, `-o /tmp/a2-{}.json`, `-o /tmp/e1.csv`, and at the end `rm -f /tmp/a2-*.json /tmp/e1.csv /tmp/e2.csv`
findings.expected: Steps that stay inside the project or a private temp directory (e.g. `mktemp -d`).
findings.actual: Fixed names in /tmp. On a shared machine (two evaluators at once, as here) runs overwrite or delete each other's files, and the A3 `cmp` can compare against another person's answer. I had to change the paths to run the steps safely.

findings.title: A6 README step does not show that the list request overlapped the export
findings.reproduction: README › A6: `for i in 1 2 3; do curl ... export.csv -o /dev/null & done; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -w '%{time_total}s ' ... ; done; echo; wait`
findings.expected: Output that shows each list request was sent and answered while an export was still streaming.
findings.actual: Only list durations are printed (5-8 ms). Export start/end times are not shown, so overlap is assumed, not demonstrated. My own timed check confirmed the overlap (list answered at 78 ms, export ended at 435 ms).
findings.suggestion: Print timestamps (e.g. `date +%s.%N`) at the start and end of the export and of each list request.

findings.title: A3 README step covers only 'different course', not 'different payload'
findings.reproduction: README › Reproducing A3 only sends `{"courseId": 3}` with key demo-par
findings.expected: The scenario says 'a different course or request payload'; the reproduction should show both.
findings.actual: The same-course payload change is not shown. I verified it myself: `{"courseId":1,"note":"x"}` with the used key -> 409, nothing written.
findings.suggestion: Add one line with the same courseId and an extra or changed field.

findings.title: README A6 does not check the CSV row set against the data
findings.reproduction: README › A6 compares e1.csv with e2.csv and counts lines only
findings.expected: A step that shows the CSV contains exactly the matching rows (e.g. compare the line count with the list `total` for the same query).
findings.actual: Only the two exports are compared and the line count is printed against a hard-coded 25,481. My own DB comparison found the set and the order correct.

findings.title: CSV and list show identical local times for two different instants at the DST fold, with no offset
findings.expected: Distinguishable times (or an offset column) for EAST-0000003 (2026-04-04T15:30Z) and EAST-0000004 (2026-04-04T16:30Z).
findings.actual: Both rows print '2026-04-05 02:30' in the CSV and in the list. Only the detail drawer adds 'UTC+11:00' / 'UTC+10:00'. This is correct local wall-clock time but ambiguous; the requirement does not ask for more.
findings.suggestion: Optionally add the UTC offset or an ISO UTC column to the CSV.

findings.title: Unknown query parameters are silently ignored despite README wording
findings.expected: README section 5: 'Query parameters are validated: an unknown value is a 400, never silently ignored'. A reader may expect unknown parameter names to be refused as well.
findings.actual: 200; `foo` and `tenant` are ignored (harmless for isolation, because the tenant is never read from the query). Only unknown values of known parameters (e.g. sort=bogus) are 400.
findings.suggestion: Say 'unknown value of a known parameter', or reject unknown parameter names.

findings.title: --clear leaves the database file at full size
findings.reproduction: `npm run generate:east` then `npm run generate:east -- --clear`; `ls -la data/`
findings.expected: Not required, but the README says `--clear` 'leaves exactly the rows that were there without it'.
findings.actual: The rows are restored, but cert-admin.sqlite stays at about 88 MB (plus a 16 MB WAL) until `npm run db:reset`.

not_checked: `npm test` and the repository's own tests (deliberately not used as evidence; only the single A5 test the README points to was run, to follow the README)
Behaviour with two server processes on one database (README claims cross-process safety for A2/A7)
UI 'Retry safely' flow after a lost answer, and reload persistence of the bulk-issue attempt
Export timing under heavier concurrent load (more than 3 simultaneous full exports); all measured exports were under 0.6 s on this shared machine, so no repeat was needed
Node 20 / the node:sqlite fallback driver (only better-sqlite3 on Node 22.23.5 was used)
`npm run dev` and the PORT/HOST settings
A6 with a seed other than the default (`--seed N`) or a count other than 100,000
